messages:
incident-bot: Pager — elevated 5xx + timeouts observed on /v1/generate (us-west-2). 5xx spike: 8% over 5m, overall error rate trending up, tail latency increasing. Triggered paging. @oncall-sre-1 paging now.

oncall-sre-1: taking pager, looking. first check: are we seeing gateway 502s or backend 5xx?

eng-runtime: backend model-serving is returning 502/504s at the gateway. Looks like the scheduler batching queue is backing up — a few pods show queue depth >> normal and enqueue latency high. KV cache KV-growth also trending.

oncall-sre-1: copy. listing scheduler pods and queue sizes now.

eng-runtime: logs show repeated `batch_enqueue_timeout` and `hol_lock_wait` spikes. sample log:
```
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z scheduler[replica-7]: WARN enqueue_delay=1234ms queue_len=112 hol_lock_wait=890ms
2026-03-15T18:02:13Z gateway: upstream_timeout for req id=... status=504
```

oncall-sre-1: running quick health commands.

oncall-sre-1: `kubectl top pods -n redwood-scheduler` shows one node at 98% GPU mem, rest near 70%. Scheduler replicas=4. Batching throughput suddenly increased — looks like a traffic surge with many long-context requests causing head-of-line blocking.

leo: spike source? any customer rollouts or synthetic tests?

priya: I see a spike from a small number of customer keys — high token-per-request patterns. Could be an integration gone noisy. Filtering by api key now.

oncall-sre-1: mitigation plan: 1) enable immediate routing fallback to smaller model variant for hosted-tier, 2) reduce max_batch_size and per-batch timeout to force faster flush, 3) scale scheduler replicas, 4) temporarily disable prefix caching for the heavy keys to reduce KV pressure. Executing in that order.

eng-runtime: applying config change: set `max_batch_size=32 -> 16` and `batch_timeout_ms=200 -> 120` for /v1/generate route. Pushing via runtime-config.

eng-runtime: scaled scheduler deployment from 4 -> 10 replicas (horizontal). watch for backlog drop.

oncall-sre-1: routing fallback enabled for default API key: route to model:redwood-small-quant when queue_depth>80.

priya: started throttling the noisy API keys at the gateway (rate limit 10r/s) to protect shared pool.

amanda: drafting customer notification for status page: short note + ETA. Will post after we verify impact reduction.

svc-status-bot: Status update posted: "Investigating — Elevated error rates for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Engineers responding. Some customers may experience timeouts or 5xx. Updates every 15 minutes."

eng-runtime: backlog is starting to fall. queue_len per pod down from 110 to ~30 in 2m since scaling + batch size change. 5xx rate dropping from 8% -> 3.2% and latency p95 improving.

oncall-sre-1: doing a controlled restart of replica-7 (highest queue_len) to clear any stuck state.

eng-runtime: restart done. replica-7 rejoined healthy. KV cache growth rate decreased after disabling cache for noisy keys.

oncall-sre-1: summary so far: root cause appears to be a concentrated traffic pattern of very long-context prompts (high token-per-request) from a small set of keys that caused continuous large batches and head-of-line blocking. The scheduler's batching heuristics plus caching kept long-running batches in front of short requests. Combined with slow KV growth the queue became saturated and upstream gateway timed out.

leo: next actions: 1) add short-term rule to prefer low-latency small batches for interactive routes (prefer flush on small requests), 2) engineering follow-up to improve HOL avoidance in scheduler, 3) product to contact affected customers.

amanda: status page update and customer note sent: short, apologies, mitigation in place, ask to contact support if still seeing errors.

sre-manager: good mitigation and comms. ensure we capture exact API keys and throttle policy for postmortem. assign owners for follow-ups.

oncall-sre-1: will keep this thread open for 30m of stable metrics. switching pager to monitoring watchlist. final checks: 5xx now ~1.1%, p95 latency back to normal.

eng-runtime: config changes recorded in runtime-config v2026-03-15-01. Follow-up tasks: add early-eviction for batches older than 400ms, add per-key throttling queue at gateway, improve telemetry to detect growing token-per-request trends earlier.

amanda: postmortem note to be created: include timeline, noisy keys list, mitigations, and customer impact summary. Putting owners: eng-runtime (remediation), product (customer outreach), infra (autoscale policy tweak).

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> monitoring. Please file postmortem within 72 hours and tag `incidents/batching`. :white_check_mark:
